title: Prepaid Dental HMO Plans Evidence of Coverage, Article 2: Eligibility to Enroll and Coverage Effective Date
content:
## Article 2 — Eligibility to Enroll and Coverage Effective Date (Prepaid Dental HMO Plans)

**2.1 Who may be enrolled.** A DHMO enrollment may be opened only for a subscriber residing in one of the service area states, for a plan whose entry gate admits the market, and with an assigned primary care dentist who holds an active Cascade DHMO Primary Care Dentist Agreement with an open panel in the subscriber's state.

**2.2 Orthodontic rider exclusion.** A person who holds an applied or active Cascade orthodontic rider may not enroll in a DHMO, because the rider and the DHMO orthodontic copay schedule are mutually exclusive.

**2.3 Effective date.** Individual applications take effect on the first of the month following receipt and group enrollments on the group's effective dates; there is no waiting period, deductible or annual maximum.

**2.4 Start of coverage.** Coverage starts on the coverage effective date once the binder premium is received on the funding billing account. An accepted application stands as applied until then, and becomes active on the coverage effective date once the binder premium has been received and a primary care dentist has been assigned.

### 2.5 Conditions for opening an enrollment

Every condition must hold; if any one fails, the enrollment may not be opened.

| Condition | What it turns on |
|---|---|
| Residence | The subscriber resides in one of the service area states of the plan. |
| Market | The entry gate of the plan elected admits the market of the enrollment (individual or group). |
| Primary care dentist | The assigned dentist holds a Cascade DHMO Primary Care Dentist Agreement that is active, with a panel that is open, in the subscriber's state. |
| No open orthodontic rider | The person being enrolled holds no Cascade orthodontic rider that is applied or active. |

### 2.6 How the orthodontic rider exclusion is established

- **Whose record decides.** The company's own records of Cascade orthodontic riders decide this condition, read before the enrollment is opened; it is not settled by what the applicant says.
- **Which rider is the person's.** A rider belongs to the person being enrolled when the covered person on the rider has the same name and the same date of birth as the person named on the DHMO enrollment.
- **Which states allow enrollment.** A rider of that person in the state terminated or cancelled does not stand in the way. A rider of that person that is applied or active does.

| The person's Cascade orthodontic rider is… | DHMO enrollment of that person |
|---|---|
| applied | Not permitted |
| active | Not permitted |
| terminated | Not barred by this condition |
| cancelled | Not barred by this condition |

A rider recorded for a different person — a different name or a different date of birth — is not that person's rider.

### 2.7 Effective date cases (hypothetical dates)

- An individual application received on 17 March takes effect on 1 April, the first of the month following receipt.
- An individual application received on 1 March takes effect on 1 April.
- An individual application received on 31 March takes effect on 1 April; one received on 1 April takes effect on 1 May.
- A group enrollment takes effect on the group's effective dates, not on the first of the month following receipt.
- On the effective date, coverage starts once the binder premium has been received on the funding billing account.
